The Tax Commissioner has Suite 105 on the ground floor of the Administration Building, 201 N. Davis Street, Nashville, Georgia 31639. For a bill or a payment, call (229) 686-7461. Visitors are welcome on weekdays from eight until five. Real property, personal property, mobile home, motor vehicle and timber tax all run through this one office.

Value is a different office's job. Berrien's Board of Tax Assessors sets it and takes homestead applications, and the commissioner's staff will direct you there if you are unsure.

  • Tax Commissioner: bills, receipts, help paying, liens
  • Tax Assessor: values, returns, homestead and other exemptions
  • Clerk of Superior Court: warranty deed copies from the courthouse deed room

Berrien covers 458 square miles of rural south central Georgia, and a single school system, the Berrien County School District, serves every address. The headcount went from 19,286 in 2010 down to 18,160, then back up to an estimated 18,932 for 2025. Nearly three quarters of residents in 2020 lived outside urban areas, so most owners hold rural parcels rather than town lots.

The county has 8,328 housing units in 2025 and a 71.0 percent owner rate. Median household income is $52,876, the middle owner-occupied value is $131,600 and middle gross rent is $782 a month. Only 115 building permits were issued in 2025, so most listings are older farmhouses and country lots, and buyers price them that way.

Every year, houses, land and business equipment are due November 15. Mobile and manufactured homes come due April 1 instead, and vehicles follow the owner's birthday.

Each month of delay adds 1% interest. If the bill is still open three months past the deadline, a flat 10% penalty is added. At 30 days overdue, the office can record a FiFa lien with the Clerk of Superior Court, and in the end the commissioner may levy on the parcel.

Parcel searches and online payments run on the GovtWindow platform, and the help desk number is (877) 575-7233. Georgia classes a mobile or modular home as personal property, so a yearly return and a location permit apply, and the permit is withheld until that year's tax is paid in full. The commissioner also bills timber tax, a point that matters to anyone selling acreage.

Berrien County payment calendar and late charges
Account typeDueIf late
Real estate and business personal propertyNovember 151% a month, then 10% after 90 days
Mobile and manufactured homesApril 1Location permit needs tax paid in full
Motor vehiclesOwner's birthdayCollected by the same office

Georgia taxes 40% of market value, and Berrien's county commissioners and school board each pick a millage yearly. The sequence is short: start from assessed value, subtract exemptions to reach net taxable value, then multiply by the mills. Each mill raises a dollar on every $1,000 of that net figure.

Rather than guess, ask the commissioner for the millage on your parcel. Statements are mailed to the owner, so a lender that escrows needs a copy. Check that your servicer has the Berrien bill, and keep your own copy for the closing file.

  • Returns: you may state your own value at any point in the first three months of the year
  • Notice: the assessors send one when their value differs from the return
  • Bill: the commissioner applies the mills to net taxable value

The test is ownership and residence on New Year's Day. Mail or deliver the application to the tax assessor's office so it is received before April 1. Filing is open all year, yet a late application only helps the next tax year, so do not wait.

Selling the house ends your claim, and the buyer applies on their own. Mention it to the buyer's agent so the new owner knows to file before April 1.

Once approved, the exemption continues each year at that address. If you move to a different Berrien house, you file again. Homeowners at 62 may apply for an added exemption, and business personal property can qualify for freeport relief. The dollar figures change with legislation, so the assessors are the source for current amounts.

Count 45 days from the notice date. Either the county Board of Equalization or an arbitrator hears the case, and a disappointed owner can send the Board of Tax Assessors written notice of a move to superior court.

If you appeal a market value by mail, the postmark must be no later than day 45. Tax that was collected in error or illegally can be recovered with a written claim made within three years of payment. Keep your receipts, since the three years run from the day you paid.

Country land is common here, and it brings a few extra checks. Timber is taxed and billed by the commissioner, so a seller with standing trees should ask whether any timber tax is open. A mobile home on the land is a separate account with its own April 1 deadline and its own permit.

List each account when you talk to the buyer's side. A clean payoff on the house alone does not tell the title company that the mobile home or timber account is also paid, and a missed one can delay a closing. If the deed came to you through an estate, ask the commissioner whether the bills for earlier years went to a prior owner, and settle them all in one visit so the record is complete before you sign.

Ahead of any offer, get the balance from the commissioner in writing and find out who the bill is addressed to. January 1 ownership drives the statement, which means yours may arrive even after a fall closing. How the year's tax is split between you and the buyer will be laid out by your closing agent.

A recorded FiFa is public record, and it has to be paid off before the buyer can receive clean title. An old farmhouse with back taxes, an inherited deed or deferred repairs can still sell as is, because the payoff comes out of the sale money. Any cash buyer will want the same payoff number you hold. If the house is a rural parcel, also ask whether any timber tax or a mobile home account is attached to the same owner, since the commissioner bills those too, and settle each one before the deed is signed.

A cash sale avoids lender appraisals and repair lists, which suits a farmhouse with deferred upkeep. The tax payoff remains. You pay the balance from your proceeds at the table, and knowing the number early keeps the closing date steady.

Bring these to Suite 105: your deed or parcel number, the latest statement, any lien notice, and your closing agent's name. Get the figures in writing with the date they are good through, since interest builds monthly.

faqs.q: When does Berrien County want its property tax?
faqs.a: Real estate and business personal property are due every November 15. A mobile home account is due April 1.

faqs.q: What does overdue Berrien County tax cost?
faqs.a: You pay 1% interest per month starting at the due date, plus a 10% penalty after 90 days of nonpayment.

faqs.q: Where is the Berrien County tax office?
faqs.a: Suite 105 of the Administration Building, 201 N. Davis Street, Nashville. Call (229) 686-7461; the office keeps weekday hours of 8 to 5.

faqs.q: How fast must a Berrien County assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. Either the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator hears it.

faqs.q: Does the Berrien tax bill go to my lender?
faqs.a: No, statements are mailed to owners alone. With an escrow account, send the bill along or check that the servicer is paying.
